title: Rule of Law and the Welfare State — Limits of Dicey

content.overview: The welfare state expands administrative power to deliver social benefits and regulation. Dicey's suspicion of wide discretion fits uneasily with welfare administration. Modern rule-of-law thinking accepts authorised discretion but insists on fairness, non-arbitrariness and review.
content.glance: Identify the welfare power and its statutory source; test procedural fairness and non-arbitrariness; avoid treating welfare discretion as either unlimited or as pure private largesse.
content.study: Welfare administration necessarily involves discretionary allocation of benefits and burdens. The rule of law does not forbid discretion; it requires that discretion be authorised, guided by relevant criteria, exercised fairly and open to review. Cases on livelihood, benefits and procedural due process illustrate how Article 14 and Article 21 discipline welfare power without freezing policy. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the Constitution and the specific welfare statute. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Welfare State and Discretion
sections.body: Social regulation and benefits require flexible administrative power.

sections.heading: Limits of Classical Dicey
sections.body: Strict hostility to discretion cannot describe modern welfare administration.

sections.heading: Fairness and Non-Arbitrariness
sections.body: Hearing, relevant considerations and reasoned decisions discipline welfare power.

sections.heading: Livelihood and Article 21
sections.body: Where welfare action affects livelihood or basic needs, procedural and substantive constraints intensify.

sections.heading: Remedies
sections.body: Writs and statutory appeals enforce legal limits on welfare administration.

examples.title: Benefit denial without hearing
examples.body: A welfare benefit is cancelled without notice or opportunity to respond. Fairness and non-arbitrariness constraints are engaged.

examples.title: Livelihood impact
examples.body: An administrative measure threatens livelihood. Article 21 analysis of fair procedure intensifies alongside Article 14.

hypotheticals.question: Are welfare benefits pure gifts beyond legal control?
hypotheticals.analysis: Where statute and Constitution structure the scheme, legal standards apply.

hypotheticals.question: Does any denial of benefit violate Article 21?
hypotheticals.analysis: Article 21 analysis depends on the interest affected and the fairness of process.

misconceptions.trap: Welfare benefits are pure gifts beyond legal control.
misconceptions.correction: Where statute and Constitution structure the scheme, legal standards apply.

misconceptions.trap: Any denial of benefit violates Article 21.
misconceptions.correction: Article 21 analysis depends on the interest affected and the fairness of process.

cases.name: D.S. Nakara v Union of India
cases.facts: Pension classification challenge in a welfare context.
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court applied equality principles to the welfare classification under challenge.
cases.holding: The Court disposed of the matter on equality standards.
cases.relevance: Authority already in the file on welfare and equality.

cases.name: Olga Tellis v Bombay Municipal Corporation
cases.facts: Pavement dwellers challenged eviction affecting livelihood.
cases.issue: Whether livelihood interests engage Article 21 procedural protections.
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court linked livelihood to Article 21 and required fairness before deprivation.
cases.holding: Procedural protections were required before eviction on the facts.
cases.relevance: Authority already in the file on livelihood and Article 21.

cases.name: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
cases.facts: Passport impounded without adequate opportunity and reasons.
cases.issue: What standard of fairness governs State action affecting personal liberty?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Procedure affecting Article 21 liberty must be fair, just and reasonable.
cases.holding: The Court constitutionalised procedural fairness and reasonableness.
cases.relevance: Authority already in the file on fairness and Article 21.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a welfare rule-of-law problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify welfare power and statute. II. Test fairness and non-arbitrariness. III. Apply Article 21 if livelihood/liberty engaged. IV. Formulate remedy.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Statutory source; fairness defect; Article 14/21 analysis; precise relief.

examTips: State tension between Dicey and welfare discretion.
Apply fairness and Article 21 where livelihood is engaged.
Do not treat benefits as pure gifts.

Dicey's model needs adaptation, not abandonment of legality.
